title: Make location information useful and current

scenes.title: Make location information useful and current
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will make location information useful and current. A map can mislead when old positions remain visible or useful sites and reference layers are missing. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: A department adds its stations and hospitals as points of interest and lets personnel locations expire after 60 minutes so old positions disappear. A current map shows where responders and apparatus are and puts important locations in front of dispatchers. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Mapping
scenes.narration: Mapping. The live map of personnel, units and calls. Set how long locations stay on the map in the mapping settings. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Points of Interest
scenes.narration: Points of Interest. Points of interest such as stations, hospitals and hydrants. Add the locations dispatchers need to see. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Weather zones and alerts
scenes.narration: Weather zones and alerts. Weather alert zones and alert notifications. Draw the zones you cover and choose who is alerted.

scenes.title: Map Layers
scenes.narration: Map Layers. Add your own shapes and overlays to the map. Confirm members allow location sharing in the Responder app, and decide how long a position should stay on the map. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Live Routing
scenes.narration: Live Routing. Directions and routes for responding resources. Confirm members allow location sharing in the Responder app, and decide how long a position should stay on the map. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Custom map layers
scenes.narration: Custom map layers. Upload your own map images, such as a campus or venue map. Confirm members allow location sharing in the Responder app, and decide how long a position should stay on the map. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Indoor maps
scenes.narration: Indoor maps. Floor plans and zones for buildings. Confirm members allow location sharing in the Responder app, and decide how long a position should stay on the map. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Routes
scenes.narration: Routes. Planned routes, such as patrols, and who is assigned to them. Confirm members allow location sharing in the Responder app, and decide how long a position should stay on the map. Availability also depends on Mapping. Check access in the target department.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Review personnel and unit location-age settings. Step 2. Add stations and hospitals as points of interest. Step 3. Add a relevant map layer, planned route, or weather zone and review its audience.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Check marker age and source, POI placement, reference-layer alignment, and the intended weather-alert coverage. A common problem to watch for: Location sharing requires client permission. Uploaded floor plans are reference material; verify currency and alignment before relying on them.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Follow a sample unit and compare a recent position with a stale position. Record missing POIs and outdated reference layers. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed. Use the linked feature scripts for the detailed screen recording plan.
